svg.title: Cell processes
svg.desc: Chromosomes & genes: The nucleus contains chromosomes made of DNA. Each carries many genes. Body-cell chromosomes normally occur in pairs. A copied X is one chromosome with two joined identical copies. Grow & copy DNA: Before mitosis, the cell grows and makes more ribosomes and mitochondria. DNA replicates. DNA amount doubles. Chromosome number stays the same until the copies separate. Mitosis: The joined copies separate. A complete set moves to each end and the nucleus divides. DNA copying happens before mitosis. Daughter cells keep the parent’s chromosome number. Divide the cell: Cytoplasm and membrane divide into two genetically identical daughter cells. Needed for growth, development, repair and replacement, such as healing skin. Bacteria divide by binary fission, not mitosis. Human stem cells: Undifferentiated cells: divide and produce cells that can become specialised. Embryonic: most human cell types. Bone marrow: a limited range, including blood cells. The source determines which cells can form. Medical uses: Potentially replace insulin-producing cells in diabetes, or nerve cells in paralysis. Therapeutic cloning: an embryo has the patient’s genes. Its stem cells are not rejected by the patient’s immune system. These are potential treatments, not guaranteed cures. Benefits, risks & ethics: Benefit: replace damaged tissue. Risks: viral infection and uncontrolled division. Destroying embryos raises ethical or religious objections. Others prioritise treatment benefits. Give a reasoned judgement based on the source, benefits and risks. Plant meristems: Can form any plant cell type throughout life. Produce clones quickly and economically. Protect rare plants from extinction. Clone useful crops, such as disease-resistant varieties. Plant cells come from plant meristems, not human stem cells.
